datasets.name: Sea Proximity
datasets.description: How close an area is to the coast. Higher scores mean shorter distances to the sea.

datasets.name: Terrain Ruggedness
datasets.description: How mountainous the landscape is — captures slope and elevation variability rather than distance to a mountain range.

datasets.name: Sun Hours
datasets.description: How much sunshine an area receives over the year. Higher scores mean more sunny hours.

datasets.name: Temperature Pleasantness
datasets.description: How well the year-round climate matches a chosen region — temperature and humidity are scored independently, so hot-dry and hot-humid pick out different places. Higher scores mean the local climate is closer to your selected preset.

datasets.name: Rainfall
datasets.description: How balanced the rainfall is — moderate totals without long droughts or heavy downpours. Higher scores mean it is more in your selected range

datasets.name: Annual Greenness
datasets.description: How green and vegetated an area is across the year. Higher scores mean lusher landscapes.

datasets.name: Air Quality
datasets.description: How clean the outdoor air is, based on fine-particle pollution (PM2.5). Higher scores mean cleaner air.

sources.name: Van Donkelaar et al. global PM2.5 surfaces

datasets.name: Natural Disaster Risk
datasets.description: Overall exposure to natural hazards such as floods, earthquakes, cyclones, landslides, and wildfires. Higher scores mean safer areas.

datasets.name: Climate Vulnerability
datasets.description: How exposed a country is to the long-term impacts of climate change on food, water, health, ecosystems, and infrastructure. Higher scores mean lower vulnerability.

datasets.name: Population Density
datasets.description: How many people live per square kilometre. Higher scores mean it fits better your selected preference.

datasets.name: Urbanity
datasets.description: How much major-city life is within reach — bigger and more globally significant cities nearby raise the score more than distant or minor ones.

datasets.name: Internet Connectivity
datasets.description: How fast and reliable local internet access is. Higher scores mean better connectivity.

datasets.name: Healthcare Access
datasets.description: How quickly the nearest hospital or clinic can be reached by car. Higher scores mean shorter travel times.

sources.name: Malaria Atlas Project — Accessibility to Healthcare

datasets.name: Income
datasets.description: Average income level of residents. Higher scores mean wealthier populations.

datasets.name: Cost of Living
datasets.description: How expensive daily essentials — rent, groceries, transport — are. Higher scores mean more affordable.

sources.name: World Bank ICP Price Level Index

datasets.name: Crime Rate
datasets.description: How safe an area is from violent crime. Higher scores mean lower crime.

datasets.name: Human Freedom
datasets.description: How free the society is — democratic institutions, civil liberties, and freedom from political violence. Higher scores mean greater freedom.

datasets.name: Corruption
datasets.description: How much corruption shapes public life across government, courts, and public services. Higher scores mean less corruption.

datasets.name: Education
datasets.description: How educated the local population is, based on mean and expected years of schooling. Higher scores mean better education.

sources.name: Global Data Lab Subnational HDI v8.3

datasets.name: People Happiness
datasets.description: How happy people say they are — the Cantril ladder life-evaluation score (0 = worst possible life, 10 = best possible life), averaged over three years per country. Higher scores mean happier populations.

datasets.name: Working Hours
datasets.description: How many hours the average employed person works per week. Lower hours mean more leisure and better work-life balance, so higher scores here mean shorter working weeks.
